extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and Magma users working with finite planes and error-correcting codes
extracted.subtask_description: Reference and usage guidelines for Magma functions operating on finite projective/affine planes and for constructing and analysing linear error-correcting codes over finite fields. Contains definitions, constructors, property tests, and example usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective point coordinate normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Projective plane points correspond to equivalence classes of non-zero vectors; for P = PG(2, q) there are (q-1) non-zero vectors per point. Coordinates of points are stored and printed in normalized form so that the leftmost non-zero coordinate is 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When working in projective planes inside Magma, always expect and use normalized coordinates (leftmost non-zero coordinate equals 1). Example: vectors differing by a non-zero scalar represent the same projective point; use coercion into the point-set to normalize and compare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plane numerical invariants and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions returning numerical invariants and basic tests for a plane: Order(P) (order n of plane P), pRank(P, p) and pRank(P) (p-rank of the plane), IsDesarguesian(P) (true if Desarguesian), IsSelfDual(P) (true if projective plane is isomorphic to its dual).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Order(P) to determine n where projective plane has n^2+n+1 points/lines, or affine has n^2 points. pRank gives the p-rank used e.g. to match code dimensions. IsDesarguesian is always true for classical planes; may also be true for other definitions (example: IsDesarguesian(fp1) -> true).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subplane construction and existence conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a projective plane P and a set T of points, a smallest subplane containing T can be constructed provided T contains a quadrangle (four points with no three collinear). For affine planes a weaker requirement holds: T must contain three non-collinear points. Magma constructor: sub< P | points specification >. For classical planes over a field K, subplanes may be obtained by restricting coordinates to a subfield F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When constructing subplanes in Magma, supply points/sets/sequences to sub< >. For classical planes, use SubfieldSubplane to obtain the subplane corresponding to a subfield; coercion of points between subplane and parent plane is automatic for most functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embedding, dual and affine/projective conversion operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations that construct related planes: Dual(P) returns the dual of a projective plane; AffinePlane(P, l) removes line l to give an affine plane (returns plane, point-set, line-set, embedding map); ProjectiveEmbedding(A) returns projective completion (and embedding map).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding functions return the new plane plus its point and line sets; embedding maps let you move points/lines between affine and projective representations. Example: ProjectiveEmbedding(AP9) produced a projective plane isomorphic to original P9 with mapping m2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arcs and line-intersection classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and operations for k-arcs: a k-arc is a set of k points with no three collinear; complete k-arc cannot be extended. Lines w.r.t. an arc are classified as tangent (meets arc exactly once), secant (exactly twice), or passant/external (never). Magma functions: kArc(P,k), CompleteKArc(P,k), IsArc(P,S), IsComplete(P,A), Tangent(P,C,p), AllTangents(P,A), AllSecants(P,A), ExternalLines(P,A), AllPassants(P,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use kArc to generate arcs and AllSecants/AllTangents to investigate line intersections. Example usages show generating a 4-arc, finding its tangent at a point and enumerating its secants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conics and unitals in classical projective planes
rubrics_metrics.description: For classical projective planes over finite fields: Conic(P,S) gives the unique conic through a 5-arc (when order n>3); QuadraticForm(P,S) returns quadratic form defining that conic. For planes over GF(q^2) a unital U has q^3+1 points with every line meeting two points in U meeting q+1 points in U; Magma provides IsUnital(P,U), AllTangents(P,U), UnitalFeet(P,U,p), Interior(P,C), Knot(P,C), Exterior(P,C) (various constructions/properties depending on q odd/even).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct conics from 5-arc via Conic and get defining quadratic form via QuadraticForm. To verify and use unitals, check cardinality equals q^3+1 and use IsUnital; you can construct Steiner designs from unitals by taking blocks as line intersections of size q+1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collineation and automorphism group operations for planes
rubrics_metrics.description: Group-theoretic operations: CollineationGroup(P) (same as AutomorphismGroup(P) acting on points), PointGroup(P), LineGroup(P), IsPointTransitive(P)/IsTransitive(P)/IsLineTransitive(P) (transitivity tests), CentralCollineationGroup variants (with centre p and/or axis l), IsCentralCollineation(P,g), CollineationGroupStabilizer(P,k), CollineationSubgroup(P).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many of these functions that return groups (except LineGroup) can return up to five values: the group G, G-set action on points, G-set on lines, parent M for automorphisms represented as maps, and a transfer map t: G → M. Use FactoredOrder and Order on returned groups (examples show orders and factorizations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions between planes, designs, graphs and codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to transfer between combinatorial structures: Design(P) returns the design of points and lines of plane P; PointGraph(P), LineGraph(P) return graphs whose vertices are points or lines, with adjacency defined by incidence; IncidenceGraph(P) returns bipartite incidence graph; LinearCode(P,K) returns the linear code over field K generated by characteristic functions of the lines (equivalently rows of the incidence matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use LinearCode(P,K) to get codes from planes; the dimension equals pRank(P) in examples. Point/line/ incidence graphs and designs enable exploring relationships between planes and other combinatorial objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Linear code constructors and [n,k,d] description
rubrics_metrics.description: Linear codes are subspaces of K^n. Constructors include LinearCode(V) (from a vector subspace V ≤ K^n), LinearCode< K, n | generator specification > (construct from explicit generator vectors), LinearCode(A) (rows of matrix A), and LinearCode(P, K) (from plane or incidence structure). Linear codes are described as [n, k, d] where n = block length, k = dimension, d = minimum weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generator matrices shown in Magma output are echelonized bases of the defining subspace. Example: constructing a [6,3,3] code from three generators and verifying equivalence of different constructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codeword/vector handling and parent magma behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Codewords are implemented as ordinary vectors in Magma: coercing a length-n sequence into a code returns an element whose parent is the generic vector space K^n, not the code object C. Individual components can be modified to simulate channel errors. Membership coercion into C is allowed only for actual codewords; attempting C ! v when v ∉ C raises a runtime error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To create or manipulate vectors not in C, coerce into AmbientSpace(C) or use AmbientSpace to obtain K^n. Example shows changing a codeword component and then Syndrome showing non-membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector and codeword operations (inner products, distance, weight, syndrome, support, coordinates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions on vectors useful for coding: InnerProduct(u,v), Distance(u,v) (Hamming distance), Weight(u) (Hamming weight), Syndrome(u,C), Support(u) (set of non-zero coordinate positions), Coordinates(C,u) (coordinates of u relative to basis/information space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Syndrome(x,C) to compute syndrome without explicitly computing parity-check matrix. Support is useful for building designs from codes. Coordinates(C,u) relates vector to generator matrix; examples show Syndrome of a modified vector is non-zero demonstrating it's not in the code.

rubrics_metrics.name: General facts and accessors for linear codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessor functions: Alphabet(C)/Field(C) (underlying field), Length(C), Dimension(C), MinimumWeight(C)/MinimumDistance(C), StandardForm(C) (returns equivalent code in standard form and isomorphism), GeneratorMatrix(C), ParityCheckMatrix(C), InformationSpace(C), InformationSet(C), AllInformationSets(C), SyndromeSpace(C), VectorSpace(C), AmbientSpace(C), Generic(C), Dual(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to inspect code structure, obtain generator/parity check matrices, determine information sets, and access the ambient vector space. StandardForm returns a consistent canonical representative and an isomorphism. MinimumWeight can be computationally expensive; be aware.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boolean/property tests for codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Tests for code properties include IsCyclic(C), IsMDS(C) (maximum-distance separable, i.e., [n,k,n−k+1]), IsSelfOrthogonal(C), IsSelfDual(C), IsWeaklySelfOrthogonal(C), IsWeaklySelfDual(C).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these predicates to test algebraic and combinatorial properties; many are straightforward but MinimumWeight/MinimumDistance interacts with some bounds and may require heavier computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sphere-packing bound calculation (example: spherepacking function)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sphere-packing bound for a q-ary (n,M,2t+1) code is M * sum_{i=0..t} Binomial(n,i)*(q-1)^i ≤ q^n. Example function spherepacking(C) computes q^n minus left-hand side to measure how far a code is from perfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply to Hamming and Golay codes to verify perfectness or gap from bound (example: spherepacking(HammingCode(GF(2),3)) returns 0; Golay code returns a large positive number). Uses MinimumWeight, Length, Field, and #C.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard families of linear codes (constructors and parameters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma provides constructors for many standard codes: HammingCode(K,r) (parameters [(q^r-1)/(q-1),(q^r-1)/(q-1)-r,3]), ReedMullerCode(r,m), GolayCode(K,true/false) (extended/unextended binary/ternary Golay), ReedSolomonCode variants (by field and length), GRSCode(A,V,k) (generalized Reed-Solomon with evaluation points A and multipliers V).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer special constructors for efficiency rather than building generators by hand. Output includes generator matrix and standard parameters, e.g., Extended ternary Golay [12,6,6].

rubrics_metrics.name: Cyclic and BCH/QR code constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Cyclic code constructors: CyclicCode(u) (from generating vector), CyclicCode(n,f) (from polynomial f dividing x^n-1), CyclicCode(n,R,K) (from roots set R), BCHCode(K,n,d,b) (q-ary BCH of designed distance d with offset b), BCHCode(K,n,d) (b=1 default), QRCode(K,n) (quadratic residue codes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use polynomial or root descriptions to create cyclic codes efficiently. Examples show creating length-7 binary cyclic code using polynomials, vectors, or root sets producing equivalent codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations specific to cyclic codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations available for cyclic codes: GeneratorPolynomial(C), CheckPolynomial(C), Idempotent(C) (idempotent generator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions extract algebraic descriptions of cyclic codes useful for analysis and further algebraic manipulations (e.g., computing generator/check polynomials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternant, Goppa, Srivastava and generalized BCH constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advanced code constructors over extension fields: AlternantCode(A,Y,r) returns q-ary alternant code with parameters ≥ [n, n−mr, r+1]; GoppaCode(L,G) returns q-ary Goppa code Γ(L,G) with parameters ≥ [n, n−mr, r+1]; ChienChoyCode(P,G,n,q) returns a generalized BCH code; SrivastavaCode(A,W,mu,K) and GeneralizedSrivastavaCode(A,W,Z,t,K) return (generalized) Srivastava codes with parameter conditions on sequences A,W,Z and integers mu,t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sequences A (evaluation points) and Y/V/W/Z etc and polynomial G or parameters as required; examples include constructing a [31,16,7] Goppa code and a [15,5,7] alternant code. Ensure terms of A are distinct and non-zero constraints satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructing new codes from existing codes (code transformations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Code transformation functions: AugmentCode(C) (binary C plus all-ones vector), ExtendCode(C) (add overall parity check), ExpurgateCode(C) (binary C with only even weight codewords), LengthenCode(C) (augment then extend), DirectSum(C,D), PlotkinSum(C,D), DirectProduct(C,D), PunctureCode(C,i or S) (delete coordinates), ShortenCode(C,i or S) (delete coordinates and keep only words zero on those positions), SubfieldSubcode(C,S) (code over subfield S formed by words of C with components in S and restriction map), SubfieldSubcode(C) for prime subfield.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these operations to derive codes with desired properties (e.g., expurgation to ensure even weight, puncturing/shortening to change length/dimension). Example: ExpurgateCode applied to a Hamming code yields a code of different parameters with only even words.
